chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Al-Makhldi told us, saying: Yunus ibn al-A'la told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, saying: He told me that Amr ibn al-Harith reported that Abu Ishana al-Ma'afary told him that he heard Uqbah ibn Amer saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever has three of his progeny die (thakala), and he counts them as a reward from God, the Exalted and Mighty, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.

key_terms.ثَكَّلَ: To have children die, specifically losing three
key_terms.فَاحْتَسَبَهُمْ: And he counted them (as a reward)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for losing three children in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Urwa ibn al-A'mar, emphasizing that the martyrdom or death of three children from one's own lineage serves as a direct guarantee of Paradise, provided the parent maintains *ihtisab* (expecting reward). This specific threshold distinguishes the immense spiritual merit of enduring multiple familial losses, a concept deeply rooted in Shia traditions regarding the trials of the Imams and the faithful. The narration underscores the transformative power of patience (*sabr*) into a decisive criterion for entering Jannah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-245 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Al-Mokhledy quoted Yunus ibn Abdul Ali, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahab, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ashanat al-Ma’afery that he had heard Aqabah ibn Amer say that
God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “The Honorable the Exalted God has guaranteed Paradise for whoever three of his progeny are crucified for the sake of God.”
